exposure: Individualized mother's breastfeeding plan of care
Providing breast milk to the newborn
Comprehensive primary care follow-up at discharge
outcome: Reduced risk factors for hospital readmission (due to inadequate weight gain, dehydration, hyperbilirubinemia)
cohort: A late preterm infant born at 36 0/7 weeks' gestation, delivered via cesarean section, identified as being at risk for breastfeeding challenges, with late preterm defined as 34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks' gestation.
finding: An individualized in-hospital breastfeeding plan for late preterm infants, combined with comprehensive primary care follow-up at discharge, can reduce risk factors for readmission and promote breastfeeding success.
followup_time: From birth through discharge and post-discharge with comprehensive primary care follow-up (specific duration not mentioned).
gest_age: Late preterm infants (34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks' gestation), with the case infant at 36 0/7 weeks' gestation.
